47443ea.assunto: Receipt alerts: a second opinion on every network, checked address by address
corpo: Second security review of Oct 23, in both apps:

outside the UTXO networks, the asset that changes (or the starting balance) is read again from a provider run by a different company. On the way up the lower value counts, on the way down the higher one, and at the start both must match; without confirmation, the last seen balance stays. A single RPC can no longer invent 'Received 10,000 USDT';

UTXO networks: the seen balance is kept per address. Pinned provider and witness must match exactly, including the starting balance, and a provider that is down only silences its own addresses. On Litecoin and Dogecoin, only owners that don't read the other network come first;
price by id only while the recognition is still valid.
iOS: only the logos from the list and from Market are stored on disk; logos of unlisted tokens stay in memory only. The folder is deleted when the wallet is removed and on erase all.

4b5f68d.assunto: Receipt alerts now include passphrase wallets
corpo: On iOS and Android, wallets with a passphrase were left out of the receipt alert, so an EVM token received in one never notified. The wallet already sits in the wallet list inside the vault, and the alert file holds every watched wallet's addresses, so leaving it out protected almost nothing. It now joins like any other wallet once its words and passphrase are confirmed. The settings note says so in all 12 languages.

632ee7b.assunto: Authorized version: a list signed outside GitHub and Apple, and the alarm in the app
corpo: ReleaseKeys (P-256 keys compiled into the app, with a threshold) and ReleaseManifest (the signed manifest, checked byte by byte: unknown key, tampered text, unmet threshold and another app's list are refused).

ReleaseWatch: the installed version asks the App Store (itunes.apple.com/lookup) which is the newest and checks it against the site's list (tmzzjr.github.io/.../versoes.json). A new version outside the list or a missing list: "Update not confirmed by Escalibur"; a signature that doesn't match: "Escalibur's version list doesn't match". Without an answer, no warning.
UpdateGuard in the app: when returning to the foreground, at most every 6 hours; the notice stays in the Wallet, under the balance. UI test with -alarme-versao.

tools/versoes/versoes.swift: the key in the Secure Enclave of the owner's Mac, bound to it and to Touch ID on every signature; authorize and check the list. verificar.sh checks the site's versoes.json against the compiled keys; the site generator publishes the file.
The two new hosts in hosts.lock, in AllowedHosts and in the Privacy Policy (pt and en).

d3030c1.assunto: Bridge: USDT to Tron through Tether's own USDT0 (Legacy Mesh)
corpo: From Ethereum and Arbitrum to the Tron account of the same wallet. Tether's contracts (UsdtOFT, verified on Sourcify with an exact match, no proxy) checked on chain from two sources on each side: the token, the fee, the peer on Tron and, on Tron, the TR7NH USDT and the return peers. Nothing comes from an API: what arrives, the liquidity and the message fee come from the contract itself (quoteOFT, quoteSend). The app builds the send and reads it back through the strict decoder: Tron destination and no other, the wallet's Tron account, no options or call, change to the owner, the quoted minimum. In the plan, the contract read again, exact approve, simulation in two sources with OFTSent, and the Tron account must be under its own key. Arrival is checked by the message guid: its OFTReceived and the USDT Transfer on Tron, read from the solidified node of two providers.
Unit tests for each refusal and live tests: a plan with a real simulation on Ethereum and Arbitrum, and a real delivery on Tron found by the guid. On screen, Tron shows up in To.

Ripple's s1 and s2 servers now count as one company: if xrplcluster went down, the XRP Ledger consensus would have been Ripple agreeing with itself.

e4f6bff.assunto: Security review of Oct 23: receipt alerts, block proofs and providers
corpo: receipt alerts: a fixed provider for the whole list (salted HMAC), with no fallback. When the balance changes, a provider from another company checks both ways; without confirmation, the seen balance stays. This closes the fake alert with the fixed provider down and the one that lowers the balance only to bring it back;
alerts: an EVM token that wasn't read doesn't count as sent;
alerts: a normal wallet wins over a watch-only one with the same address;
alerts: the salt is drawn again if it's missing;
block proof: a witness from another company is required, and nothing above the tip;
status: confirmed only with two companies or with the proof, and without a tip it stays pending; status and fee ask the full providers first;
a single company in front of a network family (EndpointsFamilyTests): Solana through its own RPC, Aptos through Sentio, Litecoin between litecoinspace and Bitcore, Dogecoin through Atomic;
swap: CoW's split sample goes with the random address, and the aggregator cache works again (without the owner in the key);
price alerts: a 10^21% change no longer breaks the check.
iOS: the background alert runs at most once an hour. Android: updating replaces the 20-minute schedule with an hourly one.

ef86431.assunto: iOS and Android: Bitcoin confirmed only with an SPV proof
corpo: Coins to send and confirmed receipts require proof that the transaction is in a mined block: a Merkle path up to the header root, a header with the work of its own target and a target never easier than the floor (16x that of block 972,695), up to six chained headers, and the same block at that height from a provider run by another company when it answers. Before, a provider could invent a transaction with the right txid paying the wallet and it showed as confirmed.

Coins without proof go to the unverified ones; receipts without proof stay pending. On for Bitcoin with the app's providers; proven headers are cached for the session. Tests with real data from block 972,600.

f7de1f2.assunto: Android: Security in the iOS order, add coin sheet and relief for the main thread

Alerts with the warning bell, the bitcoin symbol and the minus in a circle; the add coin sheet with the glass OK. Send with the iOS spacing at the top and paste text only. Immutable snapshots at most five per second, so the wallet doesn't redraw everything for every network that arrives.

The work of each header is measured with scrypt (N=1024, r=1, p=1), with a floor of 16 times the target of Oct 22, 2026. Blockbook is the second company that checks the block at that height. With no proof provider online, Litecoin falls back to the previous consensus; a proof that arrives and doesn't add up is always refused. Header cache separated by network.
